public_rationale: The forecast says a major big-tech service will break in a way not quickly fixable because of AI coding tools 'at some point in the near future.' There is no firm deadline. Before the post, Amazon had incidents linked in reporting to AI coding tools, including a 13-hour AWS disruption in December 2025. Amazon called it user error, and those events predate the forecast anyway. Searches found no prolonged big-tech outage after 2026-03-24 that a postmortem or credible reporting attributes to AI-written code. Other cases, such as GitHub's 2026 outages, were linked to AI traffic load rather than AI-written code. With no deadline and no qualifying event, the forecast stays open.
limitations: Outage attribution is often contested, and companies may not disclose AI involvement.

our_interpretation: 'Major big tech service' is read as a widely used service of a large tech company (for example Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Apple).
'Isn't immediately fixable' is read as a prolonged outage or failure, many hours or more, not a brief blip.
Cause: the failure must be credibly attributed, by the company's postmortem or well-sourced reporting, to code or changes produced with AI coding tools.
'Near future' has no fixed deadline, so the forecast is open-ended. Only events after the post date count.
criteria.support_condition: After 2026-03-24, a major big-tech service suffers a prolonged failure that the company or credible reporting attributes to AI-written or AI-assisted code changes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No firm deadline exists, so the forecast cannot be contradicted by absence alone. It could only be judged failed after a deadline was agreed.
